name: Synthesis and kilogram production capacity is not secured
trigger: No named synthesis lead, validated host or three-train 1 kg production route at M2; inability to supply 180 kg within 5760 production hours by M24; or less than 75% recovered yield in the route trial.
mitigation: Use reference MOF immediately for platform/models/control; redirect already budgeted IRC researcher and technician effort to a supported composition/route in the same two families; technical scope narrows only through a logged decision. No sixth beneficiary or outsourced core synthesis.
consequence: Up to 3 months within pre-M24 work; defined cost exposure EUR30k direct, requiring partner confirmation before release.

name: Shaping loses accessible capacity or conductance
trigger: Less than 80% powder working capacity, more than 10% lot CV, excessive attrition or a vapour pressure loss that prevents the common service at M10/M18.
impact: A transport route cannot sustain useful duty.
mitigation: Reduce binder or compaction, shorten diffusion length, or reopen one of the three already tested settings; retain both granule and conductive routes as comparative experiments even if one has a narrow earned domain.
consequence: One manufacturing iteration in M19-M24; up to EUR15k direct from the defined cartridge/rework work, with reduction elsewhere if needed.

name: Models are non-identifiable or do not transfer
trigger: Two mechanisms remain equivalent across thickness/contact/history tests, or heat NRMSE exceeds 10% rated duty on whole-run holdouts at M18/M22.
impact: Mechanism attribution and adaptive-model reliability weaken.
mitigation: Use the simplest sufficient state, add the bounded independent structural/population observation already budgeted, and restrict the predictive domain; corrections get a new version and unused repeat histories.
consequence: Up to 2 months and EUR10k direct equivalent effort/access, using the existing observation allocation.

name: RL does not outperform economic MPC
trigger: At M32 the paired independent-block uncertainty interval includes zero benefit, constraint reliability is worse, or inference exceeds its timing limit.
mitigation: Retain the RL-versus-MPC result and causal action/log analysis; deploy MPC while reporting where RL is useful, equivalent or dominated. Do not retune on final challenges.
consequence: No critical-path delay or extra budget; analysis remains in T5.3.

name: Auxiliary electricity cancels useful gains
trigger: Metered active-mode cost/exergy exceeds passive operation at equal service, or compression/circulation consumes the predicted margin at M16/M22.
impact: Net resource advantage or attainable service shrinks.
mitigation: Map bypass, circulation-only and compression-only domains; reduce pressure/conductance losses or duty; report feasible service and separate drive heat/electricity instead of a net-saving claim where services differ.
consequence: One component iteration, up to 2 months and EUR15k direct within T6.2 and defined consumables.

name: Rig or pressure/vapour equipment is late
trigger: M4 specification cannot secure a 10 kW module with approximately 25 kW source duty and 200-300 m3/h vapour train, or M8 metering qualification slips by more than 1 month.
impact: Identification and final validation windows contract.
mitigation: Keep digital and coupon work active on reference data; use the same-budget modular low-pressure train and qualify metering first; absorb at most two months before M24 and protect at least nine months integrated validation.
consequence: Up to 2 months and EUR20k direct rental/iteration exposure; M25-M36 window is not consumed without a revised capacity check.

name: Key staff or facilities are unavailable
trigger: A role exceeds its reserved monthly FTE, a named deputy is absent, or instrument access falls below 80% of the booked capacity for two months.
impact: Synthesis, model or validation throughput slips.
mitigation: Redistribute effort among the already budgeted staff slots of the five partners, cross-train deputies and move routine measurement blocks within the same partner infrastructure. No assumed free labour or facility.
consequence: Up to 2 months and EUR15k direct equivalent effort/access; role or access failure remains a pre-submission capacity gap.

name: Cost rates rental availability or cost eligibility differ
trigger: Personnel rates increase by more than 0.70%, reference powder exceeds approximately EUR201/kg, or combined quotes/eligibility changes consume the EUR12,775 headroom.
impact: Recommended work cannot be funded within EUR2.50m.
mitigation: Replace assumptions with partner cost sheets, consolidate standard equipment rentals, cut non-critical extra sweeps/events first and protect independent batches, three policy comparisons and reset accounting. No budget reserve is booked.
consequence: The 10 kW recommendation is EUR2,487,225. All personnel +5% plus the defined EUR274k equipment/facility/compute base +10% requires EUR2,612,600; EUR112,600 total-cost reductions would be required. No contingency is booked.

name: Water inventory or thermal closure biases comparisons
trigger: Energy residual exceeds 5%, mass residual exceeds 2%, or terminal inventory/stored-heat mismatch exceeds 2% of cycle transfer/heat.
impact: Apparent gain may be stored energy or measurement error.
mitigation: Pause comparative gain claims, run blanks and calibration, extend and meter reset, or report only bounded feasibility/transfer. Preserve rejected records.
consequence: Up to 1 month and six of the 24 reserved rerun histories; costs included in repeat/calibration allocations.

name: Powder yield or 500-cycle life misses qualification
trigger: Recovered production MOF below 75%, group-level supply below 20 kg per assembly, or more than 10% capacity loss in coupon ageing.
impact: Independent set production and lifecycle inference are at risk.
mitigation: Use the 24 kg nominal retained/spare allocation, reduce destructive tests, adjust the tested process window and report short-life limits. Do not pool separate validation groups or erase the ageing failure.
consequence: Up to 2 months and EUR10k direct equivalent rework; no new endurance claim or larger prototype is introduced.
